walkthroughs.body_html:
Kinematics — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Kinematics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Kinematics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A particle starts from rest and accelerates at 4 m/s² for 3 seconds. Final velocity is:
options: 12 m/s
7 m/s

mcqs.q: Which SUVAT equation does NOT involve t?
options: v² = u² + 2as
v = u + at
s = ut + ½at²

mcqs.q: If you've flipped a fair coin and got heads 5 times in a row, what is the probability the next flip is heads?
options: 1 because the coin has clearly been biased by the previous flips.
5, because that is the middle value.
1/2 — each flip is independent of the previous ones.
Less than 1/2, because the coin is 'due' to land on tails to balance the results.

mcqs.q: Is 2x the same as x squared (x^2)?
options: Yes, because both involve the number 2 and the letter x.
Yes, because the 2 represents how many times x appears.
1 because the coin has clearly been biased by the previous flips.
No — 2x means x + x (or 2 times x); x^2 means x times x.

mcqs.q: What is the range of the data set [4, 7, 2, 9, 5]?
options: From 2 to 9 — the range is given as two values.
1 because the coin has clearly been biased by the previous flips.
5, because that is the middle value.
7 — the largest minus the smallest (9 - 2).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Vertical motion under gravity”?
options: Displacement s (vector); velocity v = ds/dt; acceleration a = dv/dt = d²s/dt². All are vectors in 2D/3D.
Speed is scalar (magnitude of velocity). Velocity is vector — has direction.
If a depends on t: v = ∫a dt; s = ∫v dt. Use calculus rather than SUVAT.
Take a = g = 9.8 m/s² downward (or 9.81). Use SUVAT for projectiles, free fall.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Variable acceleration”?
options: Displacement s (vector); velocity v = ds/dt; acceleration a = dv/dt = d²s/dt². All are vectors in 2D/3D.
Speed is scalar (magnitude of velocity). Velocity is vector — has direction.
Take a = g = 9.8 m/s² downward (or 9.81). Use SUVAT for projectiles, free fall.
If a depends on t: v = ∫a dt; s = ∫v dt. Use calculus rather than SUVAT.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “SUVAT equations”?
options: For constant acceleration: v = u + at; s = ut + ½at²; v² = u² + 2as; s = ((u+v)/2)t. Useful when a is constant.
Speed is scalar (magnitude of velocity). Velocity is vector — has direction.
Slope = acceleration; area under graph = displacement. Helpful for visualising motion.
Take a = g = 9.8 m/s² downward (or 9.81). Use SUVAT for projectiles, free fall.
